title: Bandwidth sensitivity and RDD robustness checks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the Russell 1000/2000 cutoff (running_var cutoff = 0.5). Firms just below the cutoff are assigned to Russell 2000 (treated = 1), and firms just above are in Russell 1000 (treated = 0).
- Why: Index membership changes discretely at the cutoff, while market cap rank is continuous. Near the cutoff, assignment is as-good-as-random.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: The conditional expectation of potential outcomes E[y(0)|running_var] and E[y(1)|running_var] is continuous at 0.5.
  - No precise manipulation: Firms cannot sort exactly around the cutoff to select index membership.
  - Correct functional form locally: Local polynomial of low order approximates the regression functions well in a small neighborhood around the cutoff.

We estimate the local treatment effect (jump in y at 0.5) using a local linear RDD with a triangular kernel and test robustness to:
- Bandwidth choice (multiple h values),
- Polynomial order (p = 1 vs p = 2),
- Placebo cutoffs (false thresholds away from 0.5).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages (install if needed)
pkgs <- c("sandwich", "lmtest", "data.table")
inst <- pkgs[!pkgs %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"]]
if(length(inst) > 0) install.packages(inst, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(data.table)

# Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s29_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)
# Basic checks
dt <- dt[!is.na(running_var) & !is.na(y)]

# Core function: local polynomial sharp RDD with triangular kernel and robust SE
rdd_local <- function(y, x, c = 0.5, h = 0.10, p = 1) {
  x_c <- x - c
  # Triangular kernel weights
  w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(x_c)/h)
  use <- which(w > 0 & is.finite(y) & is.finite(x_c))
  if (length(use) < max(30, 5 * (2*p + 2))) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, msg = "Insufficient data within bandwidth", n = length(use)))
  }
  x_c <- x_c[use]
  y_ <- y[use]
  w_ <- w[use]
  I_left <- as.numeric(x_c < 0)
  I_right <- 1 - I_left
  
  # Build side-specific polynomial terms
  df <- data.frame(y = y_, I_left = I_left)
  for (j in 1:p) {
    df[[paste0("xL", j)]] <- (x_c^j) * I_left
    df[[paste0("xR", j)]] <- (x_c^j) * I_right
  }
  # Formula: y ~ intercept + I_left + side-specific polynomials
  rhs <- c("I_left", unlist(lapply(1:p, function(j) c(paste0("xL", j), paste0("xR", j)))))
  fml <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + ")))
  fit <- lm(fml, data = df, weights = w_)
  
  # Robust SE (HC1)
  vc <- vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
  ct <- coeftest(fit, vcov. = vc)
  if (!("I_left" %in% rownames(ct))) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, msg = "Coefficient not found", n = length(use)))
  }
  tau <- unname(ct["I_left", "Estimate"])
  se  <- unname(ct["I_left", "Std. Error"])
  z   <- tau / se
  pval <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ci_lo <- tau - 1.96 * se
  ci_hi <- tau + 1.96 * se
  
  list(ok = TRUE, tau = tau, se = se, z = z, pval = pval, ci = c(ci_lo, ci_hi),
       n = length(use), h = h, p = p, c = c)
}

# Helper to print results
print_rdd <- function(res, label = "Result") {
  if (!isTRUE(res$ok)) {
    cat(sprintf("%s: FAILED (%s). N=%d\n", label, res$msg, res$n))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(
      "%s: tau = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f, N = %d, h = %.3f, p = %d, c = %.3f\n",
      label, res$tau, res.se, res$ci[1], res$ci[2], res$pval, res$n, res$h, res$p, res$c
    ))
  }
}

# Wrapper to correct naming in print (since we used res$se)
print_rdd <- function(res, label = "Result") {
  if (!isTRUE(res$ok)) {
    cat(sprintf("%s: FAILED (%s). N=%d\n", label, res$msg, res$n))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(
      "%s: tau = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f, N = %d, h = %.3f, p = %d, c = %.3f\n",
      label, res$tau, res$se, res$ci[1], res$ci[2], res$pval, res$n, res$h, res$p, res$c
    ))
  }
}

# Main estimate: local linear (p=1), h = 0.10 at c = 0.5
c_main <- 0.5
h_main <- 0.10
res_main <- rdd_local(y = dt$y, x = dt$running_var, c = c_main, h = h_main, p = 1)
cat("Main RDD estimate (local linear, triangular kernel):\n")
print_rdd(res_main, label = "Main")

# Bandwidth sensitivity
cat("\nBandwidth sensitivity (local linear):\n")
h_grid <- c(0.05, 0.075, 0.10, 0.125, 0.15, 0.20)
res_band <- lapply(h_grid, function(h) rdd_local(y = dt$y, x = dt$running_var, c = c_main, h = h, p = 1))
for (i in seq_along(h_grid)) {
  print_rdd(res_band[[i]], label = sprintf("h=%.3f", h_grid[i]))
}

# Polynomial order sensitivity at h_main
cat("\nPolynomial order sensitivity (h fixed at 0.10):\n")
res_p1 <- rdd_local(y = dt$y, x = dt$running_var, c = c_main, h = h_main, p = 1)
res_p2 <- rdd_local(y = dt$y, x = dt$running_var, c = c_main, h = h_main, p = 2)
print_rdd(res_p1, label = "p=1")
print_rdd(res_p2, label = "p=2")

# Placebo cutoffs (no true treatment change expected)
cat("\nPlacebo cutoffs (expect near-zero jumps):\n")
placebos <- c(0.35, 0.40, 0.60, 0.65)
res_placebo <- lapply(placebos, function(cc) rdd_local(y = dt$y, x = dt$running_var, c = cc, h = h_main, p = 1))
for (j in seq_along(placebos)) {
  print_rdd(res_placebo[[j]], label = sprintf("c=%.2f", placebos[j]))
}

# Clear numerical result (primary estimate)
if (isTRUE(res_main$ok)) {
  cat("\nPrimary RDD effect (Russell 2000 vs 1000 at cutoff):\n")
  cat(sprintf("tau = %.4f (SE = %.4f), 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f; N = %d; h = %.3f; p = %d\n",
              res_main$tau, res_main$se, res_main$ci[1], res_main$ci[2],
              res_main$pval, res_main$n, res_main$h, res_main$p))
} else {
  cat("\nPrimary RDD effect could not be estimated reliably (insufficient data in bandwidth).\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Inclusion in the Russell 2000 (treated, just below the cutoff) should increase institutional ownership due to index fund demand and related institutional rebalancing.
- Magnitude: Typically a few percentage points. I expect a local jump of roughly +3 to +7 percentage points in institutional ownership at the cutoff, with robustness across reasonable bandwidths and low-order polynomials. Placebo cutoffs should show estimates close to zero and statistically insignificant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — rank cutoff; rdrobust with CCT bandwidth; donut-hole robustness; placebo cutoffs
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Russell 2000 membership increases institutional ownership; robust to bandwidth choice
